procedural_observations.method: Six pre-recorded Pepper robot videos composited over corn-maze footage; participants chose potential trust-repair strategies after a depicted mistake.
procedural_observations.recruitment: Prolific Academic, online Qualtrics; five-minute study
procedural_observations.E2_implication: Video included task-direction utterances but response task was judging appropriate repair options; R006 to assess whether operational message-action criterion is satisfied.

procedural_observations.method: Physical room maze with Pepper teleoperated by investigator; participants outside maze heard spoken options, recommendations, mistakes and repair utterances; directional choice submitted via keyboard.
procedural_observations.recruitment: Campus flyers and word of mouth; in-person six-condition between-subject design, 10 per cell
procedural_observations.E2_implication: Spoken state/options and path recommendations visibly influence participant choices; supports full-text E2 assessment by R006, not canonical eligibility.

detailed_findings.statement: Robot enumerated possible paths and recommended directions; task had decision junctions and deliberately incorrect guidance followed by apology-like/justification/promise/denial repair language.

Article describes default Pepper voice versus custom TTS; in-person participants wore noise-cancelling headphones and saw subtitles plus camera view; experimenter teleoperated the robot; audio stimuli not audited.

2025 publication describes a separate in-person maze procedure and a video pilot and cites Romeo et al. 2023; participant overlap or pilot stimulus reuse across publications not determined without 2023 full text and both supplements.
